In a quiet forest lived a tortoise named Theo, whose slow pace earned him respect but also quiet mockery. One day, he stumbled upon a shimmering feather that whispered, “Wings are for those who dare to rise.” Theo, undeterred by his size, spent months studying birds, building clumsy wings from leaves and twigs. Though his first attempts ended in tumbles, he persisted, believing flight was not a gift but a skill to learn. Safe  

On the hundredth try, Theo lifted off, soaring above the treetops. He marveled at the world from above—rivers like silver threads, distant mountains, and the sun’s golden dance. Yet as he glided, he noticed a fledgling hawk struggling to fly. Theo landed beside it, sharing his own lessons. “Speed isn’t everything,” he said. “Even the slowest can learn to rise if they never stop trying.” Safe  

Theo returned to the forest, no longer just a tortoise but a teacher. He built a small academy where creatures of all speeds practiced courage and patience. The moral? “The sky belongs to those who believe in their own wings—not the size of their stride.” Safe
